messages.subject: Issues regarding SECR with covariates.
parts:
Dear All, 
I hope this message finds you well. I am currently learning how to run Spatially Explicit Capture-Recapture (SECR) models with covariates, but I am new to this type of analysis and would greatly appreciate your guidance.

I have data files including a capture file, trap file, and covariates in the format mentioned below. Could you kindly help me with the necessary code or resources to help me set up and run SECR models with covariates for a single site?

#capture
Site  ID  Occasion  Trapid
 1         1        3               8
 1          2       9               14

#trap
Site     Trapid   x     y     1  2  3   4  5  6  7 

#covarites
x y  cov1  cov2  cov3 

Thank you for your time and support.

Best regards,
Deepali Chatrath

messages.author: 118cea91a1619106
messages.subject: Re: Issues regarding SECR with covariates.
parts:
Hello Deepali
There are several kinds of covariate. I assume from your example that you are talking about spatial covariates of density. These are 'mask' covariates. Their input is covered in the documents secr-habitatmasks.pdf and secr-densitysurfaces.pdf available from the Density website.
Murray

messages.subject: Re: Issues regarding SECR with covariates.
parts:
Hi,  
Thank you for sending the document links. I appreciate it! 
I am working on SECR on a single site with covariates. However, I’m still encountering some errors in attaching covariates to the mask.  I have used the following code:


library(secr)
library(sf)
library(ggplot2)
tmp <- read.csv("trap.csv",head = T)
names(tmp)
cameratrap <- read.traps(data = tmp[,2:4], trapID = 'trap_id', detector = "count")
usage(cameratrap) <- tmp[,5:15]
row.names(cameratrap) <- tmp$trap_id
cameratrap <- split(cameratrap, tmp$site) 
##############capture file
capture.file <- read.csv("capt.csv", head = T)
head(capture.file)

#with occasions
CH <- make.capthist(capture.file, cameratrap[[1]])
TCH<-reduce(CH, by = 'all', outputdetector = 'count', dropunused = FALSE, verify = TRUE)
summary(TCH, terse = T)
plot(TCH)
thab<-sf::st_read("mask.shp")
str(thab)
mask <- make.mask(traps(TCH), spacing = 500, type = 'trapbuffer', buffer = 5000)

covariates<- read.csv("cov.csv", head = TRUE)
str(covariates)
summary(covariates)

tmp1 <- read.mask(data = covariates, spacing = 500)
print(tmp1)

cov<- addCovariates (mask, tmp1, columns = NULL, strict = FALSE, replace = FALSE)
colnames(tmp1)

sapply(xmask, nrow)

for addCovariates it shows only x and y in column heads and not the rest of the covariates (cov1, cov2, cov3), sapply(xmask, nrow) this shows x and y as null.

Could you please help me troubleshoot this?  

Regards
Deepali Chatrath

messages.author: 118cea91a1619106
messages.subject: Re: Issues regarding SECR with covariates.
parts:
If 'mask' is a mask object and say 'covar' is a dataframe of covariates, one row for each row in 'mask' then
covariates(mask) <- covar
adds the covariates to the mask. No need for addCovariates that is used to match locations.
